claim: Gao et al (JFE 2018): S&P 500 ETF 1993-2013, the first half-hour return (measured from previous close) predicts the last half-hour return; stronger on volatile, high-volume, recession and major macro-news days; also in ten other ETFs. Effect is in-sample statistical; no trading rule or costs in abstract.
quote: the first half-hour return on the market as measured from the previous day’s market close predicts the last half-hour return.
title: Market intraday momentum (JFE abstract, RePEc)

claim: CXO summary of Gao-Han-Zhou working paper: SPY first half-hour return predicts last half-hour return with out-of-sample R-squared 0.018; hold SPY if first half-hour positive else cash gave 6.3% vs -0.5% gross annual return, Jan 1999-Dec 2012, gross of costs. Sample ends 2012 (old).
quote: SPY first half-hour returns predict last half-hour returns with R-squared 0.018 out-of-sample, generating 6.3% vs -0.5% gross annual return
title: CXO Advisory: First and Last Half-Hours of Trading Linked

claim: Gao-Han-Zhou working-paper (via CXO): predictability strengthens with volatility; R-squared about 0.02 for first half-hour alone (SPY, 1999-2012), 0.035 combined with 12th half-hour, 0.048 when first-half-hour volatility high.
quote: When first half-hour return volatility is high, the the combined first and 12th half-hour returns predict last half-hour return with R-squared 0.048.
title: CXO Advisory: First and Last Half-Hours of Trading Linked

claim: Zarattini & Aziz 5-minute ORB on QQQ (Jan 2016-Feb 2023, 1,795 trades): 33.2% vs 14.9% CAGR for buy-and-hold, zero slippage; in-sample, no spread; 1% risk per trade, 4x leverage; exit = stop at opposite end of first 5-min bar or 4:00PM close.
quote: outperformed buy-and-hold QQQ (33.2% vs 14.9% CAGR; Jan 2016–Feb 2023; 1,795 trades; zero slippage assumed)
title: CXO Advisory: Day Trading with an Opening Range Breakout Strategy (summary of SSRN 4416622)

claim: Independent blog replication of Zarattini-Aziz ORB on NQ, SPX, Dow, DAX, FTSE CFDs, Jan 2015-Jun 2026 (minute data, ~2,900 sessions each): gross +0.131 R on NQ reproduces the paper, but net of spread/slippage NQ is +0.002 R and four of five markets are negative; no market significantly positive net.
quote: Gross yes: +0.131 R on NQ, as in the paper. Net no: no market is distinguishable from zero, four of five are negative.
title: The opening-range breakout paper, replicated on five indices: gross reproduced, net zero (MQL5 blog)

claim: Same replication: ORB first-candle direction beats a random-direction bracket by +0.10 to +0.13 R (|t|>=2) in NQ, DAX, FTSE; out-of-sample years 2021-2026 give at most +0.06 R net on NQ; rule negative in all markets 2015-2017. Index CFDs not SPY/QQQ options; costs modelled as fixed point costs.
quote: the out-of-sample years 2021 to 2026 give +0.06 R on NQ at best.
title: The opening-range breakout paper, replicated on five indices: gross reproduced, net zero (MQL5 blog)

claim: Original paper characteristics per replicator: 24% hit rate, +0.13 R per trade, stop at other side of first candle, target 10x risk or session close; charges commission but no spread or slippage; no out-of-sample period.
quote: It charges commission but no spread and no slippage, and it has no out-of-sample period.
title: The opening-range breakout paper, replicated on five indices: gross reproduced, net zero (MQL5 blog)

claim: Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz: 5-min ORB on 7,000+ US stocks 2016-2023; top-20 'Stocks in Play' portfolio net total over 1,600%, Sharpe 2.81, alpha 36%, after transaction costs; stocks in play = abnormal activity (news). Multiple positions per day, in-sample, working paper; relevant to single large stocks only partly.
quote: A portfolio that consisted of the top 20 Stocks in Play achieved a total net performance of over 1,600%, with a Sharpe ratio of 2.81, and an annualized alpha of 36%.
title: A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market (Swiss Finance Institute RP 24-98)

claim: Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon SPY noise-area intraday momentum (2007-early 2024): 1,985% total return net of costs, 19.6% annualised, Sharpe 1.33; signals checked every 30 min, VWAP/noise-boundary trailing stop, flat at close; includes commissions and slippage; in-sample working paper (can enter multiple times).
quote: From 2007 to early 2024, the resulting intraday momentum portfolio achieved a total return of 1,985% (net of costs), an annualized return of 19.6%, and a Sharpe Ratio of 1.33.
title: Beat the Market: An Effective Intraday Momentum Strategy for S&P500 ETF (SPY) (SFI RP 24-97)

claim: SPY opening gap vs open-to-close return, Jan 1993-Mar 2025: correlation 0.01, i.e. neither reversal nor continuation on average; descriptive, not a trading test.
quote: SPY opening gaps showed little tendency toward reversal or continuation of the gap through the rest of the trading day (correlation 0.01 between gap and open-to-close return; Jan 1993–Mar 2025
title: CXO Advisory: Gap Reversal or Continuation?

claim: QuantConnect replication of Gao et al ETF intraday momentum, 2015-Aug 2020: strategy Sharpe lower than benchmark over the backtest and the post-2020-crash recovery, but 1.452 Sharpe during the 2020 crash; supports vol-regime dependence, weak overall.
quote: the strategy has a lower Sharpe ratio during the backtesting period and during the recovery from the 2020 stock market crash.
title: QuantConnect Research: Intraday ETF Momentum
